definitions:
N1B step 4 (CPU, local): activation-based (Goodfire-style dataset-example) labels for the 192 fixed neurons / 384
poles, and validation of the tool's static INPUT-side label gate_trigger_tokens = unembed(W_gate[i] @ J++[l].T).

PRE-STATED PREDICTIONS (copied from N1B_02_acts.py, written before any activation was recorded):
 P1 Strong events: g>0 and sign(act)=sign(u); >50% of neurons bipolar at the 30% criterion, ~30% at 50%.
 P2 Empirical input-token labels concentrated at L10-20, diffuse at L45-57.
 P3 G_jpp precision@10 vs empirical top-50 input tokens ~ permutation null (lift CI includes 1) at most layers.
 P4 G_naive (embedding match) beats G_jpp at L10-20, ~null late.
 P5 (static job) G_jpp top-10 overlaps strongly with the random-isotropic J++ prior and is shared across neurons.

Definitions
 - pole s in {+1,-1}; s*act > 0 means the pole is active (pole + = mlp_act > 0).
 - top positions of a pole: top 1% of all non-BOS positions ranked by s*act, restricted to s*act > 0.
 - input label: counts of CURRENT tokens at top positions; output-empirical label: counts of NEXT tokens (within chunk).
 - E_count50 = top-50 tokens by count (task definition); E_enrich50 = top-50 by log-enrichment vs corpus frequency
   (count >= 3), a frequency-controlled set closer to how Goodfire-style labels are read.
 - Null: every metric is computed for all (pole of neuron i, label of neuron j) pairs in the same layer; the null is the
   mean over j != i (= exact expectation over random within-layer re-pairings, i.e. infinitely many permutations);
   a permutation p-value uses 2000 random derangements. lift = mean(metric) / mean(null). 95% bootstrap CIs over poles.
Usage: .venv/bin/python N1B_04_analyze.py

mechanism_top1pct.note: frac_g_pos over a pole's top-1% positions equals frac(sign(u)==s) by construction (s*act>0). top-1% of positions includes many weak, closed-gate (g<0) positions for sparse neurons; *_top30 and *_gt30pct_own restrict to strong events.

headline.corpus: 147,534 non-BOS positions in 1,218 chunks of <=128 tokens: 13.1k model-generated chat (96 prompts, T=0.9), 89.7k local prose/docs (/usr/share/doc READMEs etc. + package METADATA), 44.7k Python code. Top-1% = 1,476 positions per pole.
headline.tool_gate_label_precision: G_jpp (= larql_vault gate_trigger_tokens) P@10 vs empirical top-50 input tokens (strict ids): 0.0070 vs null 0.0031, lift 2.27 [1.35,3.47]; normalized-string: 0.0109 vs 0.0040 (lift 2.74 [1.68,4.08]). Per layer every diff CI includes 0 (n=48 poles/layer). Ceiling (split-half-by-document empirical labels, same metric): 0.93 vs null 0.68 (count) and 0.31 vs 0.04 (enrichment). Static label captures ~1.5-2.6% of the reproducible signal.
headline.gate_token_response: Spearman(static score, token-conditional mean gate pre-activation): G_jpp 0.061 (null -0.005; L20 0.12, L30 0.14, L40 0.10, L45-57 0.01-0.06, L10 -0.03 ~ null); G_embed (W_gate*w_pre . W_E, type-correct direct path) 0.062 (L10 0.29, L20 0.09, then ~0); G_naive 0.043. Split-half ceiling 0.74.
headline.category_error: J++ pass-through of the gate covector is beaten by the direct covector.embedding pairing at L10 (0.29 vs -0.03), gives modest signal at L20-40 (rho 0.10-0.14 vs ceiling 0.74), is ~null at L57; adding the pre-FFN norm weight (the true read covector) does not help the J++ variant (0.061 -> 0.043; L20 0.118 -> 0.002). G_jpp does not track next tokens either (P@10 vs next-token enriched sets 0.0057 vs 0.0044, n.s.).
headline.J++_prior: Gate rows through J++ have top-10 softmax mass 0.40-0.90 (median per layer), the same as isotropic random vectors (0.32-0.95); naive 0.002-0.014. 24-34% of G_jpp top-10 tokens at L45-57 are random-vector-prior tokens. 93% of G_jpp label tokens occur <3 times in the corpus.
headline.poles: 82% [77,87] of neurons have weaker-pole max >= 30% of stronger; 60% [53,68] >= 50%. The two poles of a neuron fire on near-disjoint inputs (enriched top-50 Jaccard 0.039 vs 0.024 between random neurons) -> the pole-agnostic gate label cannot describe both poles. Firing is sparse: strong pole exceeds 10% of its max on 0.03% (L10) to 1.3% (L30) of tokens.
headline.mechanism: Strong events (top-30/pole): g>0 in 72-100% (L30-50 95-100%), double-negative mass 0-2.3%. But a pole's top-1% positions include many closed-gate leak events (g<0, |gelu(g)|<=0.17) for sparse neurons: double-negative mass 13-33% at the top-1% level.
headline.output_bonus: O_jvindex (J-VINDEX) vs empirical next tokens at strong events (top-0.1%): P@10 0.020 vs null 0.003, lift 6.8 [4.0,10.2], significant at L40/L50/L55; O_naive 0.028 vs 0.010 (lift 2.8).
headline.semantic: W_E centroid cosine (static top-10 vs empirical top-20 enriched): G_jpp 0.111 vs null 0.100 (diff +0.011 [0.002,0.021]); split-half empirical ceiling diff +0.154.

predictions_scorecard.P1_bipolar: CONFIRMED (stronger than predicted: 60% at the 50% criterion vs ~30% predicted). g>0 dominance holds only for strong events, not for top-1% sets.
predictions_scorecard.P2_concentration_by_layer: NOT SUPPORTED: top-10 input tokens cover 22-29% of top-1% positions at every layer (entropy 7.7-8.3 bits); no early/late contrast.
predictions_scorecard.P3_G_jpp_null: PARTLY REFUTED statistically (pooled lift 2.3-3.1, CI excludes 1; per-layer CIs include 1), SUPPORTED practically (absolute P@10 ~0.01; ~2% of the split-half ceiling).
predictions_scorecard.P4_naive_beats_jpp_early: SUPPORTED only for pre-norm-weighted direct-embedding variants (G_embed/G_naive_pre: L10 rho 0.28-0.29); the tool's own naive variant (no w_pre) is weak at L10 (0.086). Late layers ~null for embedding variants.
predictions_scorecard.P5_jpp_prior_shared: PARTLY: peakedness identical to random vectors at all layers; prior-token overlap 24-34% at L45-57 but 0-15% at L10-40; label diversity high (79-99% unique tokens/layer).
